day_shape: 87 items dominated by IDF airstrike on Hezbollah command centre in Beirut's Dahiyeh (3 killed, 15 wounded) after Hezbollah drones and projectiles hit northern Israel, an emerging US-Iran nuclear deal with Qatari mediation, and heavy regime-channel messaging around a 'martyred' Khamenei funeral.

threads.label: IDF strikes Beirut after Hezbollah projectiles
threads.summary: The IDF struck a Hezbollah command centre in Dahiyeh, Beirut after Hezbollah launched three projectiles and multiple drones at northern Israel, with Lebanon's NNA reporting three killed and 15 wounded. Netanyahu and Katz issued a joint statement; Lebanon filed a complaint with the UN Security Council and Defa Press said the strike 'crossed Iran's red line'.

threads.label: Further drone strikes and evacuation warnings
threads.summary: The IDF reported additional suspected drone impacts in northern Israel close to the Lebanese border and warned residents of 29 southern Lebanese villages to evacuate ahead of strikes. Rocket sirens also sounded in Gaza border communities including Kfar Aza, Zimrat, Shuva and Saad.

threads.label: US-Iran nuclear deal moves toward signing
threads.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told CBS the US-Iran agreement will be signed with strict verification and no funds released until commitments are met, while Qatar sent negotiators to Iran ahead of a virtual signing. A senior Iranian official told Reuters Iran will neither produce nor acquire nuclear weapons under the drafted MOU, though Tehran signalled no final decision.

threads.label: Israeli and Iranian opposition to the deal
threads.summary: Former PM Naftali Bennett denounced Netanyahu's Iran strategy in a Times of Israel interview, and the Jerusalem Post reported Israeli ministers calling for intensified Hezbollah strikes. Iranian hardliners protested against Foreign Minister Araghchi, while Speaker Ghalibaf said on Defa Press that 'talking of continuing the path is not possible' after the Beirut strike.

threads.label: Regime unity messaging and 'martyred Imam' framing
threads.summary: Khamenei's office, Pezeshkian, judiciary chief Eje'i, Araghchi and IRGC Aerospace commander Mousavi all posted calls for national unity and warnings against 'echoing the enemy'. IRIB and Defa Press repeatedly referred to a 'martyred Imam Khamenei' and detailed Mashhad and Tehran funeral arrangements led by First VP Mohammad-Reza Aref.

threads.label: Iran domestic security and economic strain
threads.summary: Iran's banking coordination council said a cyberattack hit shared infrastructure of four major banks, while the Ministry of Intelligence announced the dismantling of a four-member 'takfiri' cell and 126 arrests linked to 'enemy street riot networks'. The Jerusalem Post reported amnesty for 139 death-row inmates, and Iran International cited the Association of Social Workers on rising child labour.

events.title_en: 56 per cent of US F-35 fighters unable to carry out missions
events.summary_en: 56 per cent of US F-35 fighters unable to carry out missions. A recent report by the US Government Accountability Office confirms that only 44 per cent of US F-35 fighters are capable of carrying out missions. Additionally, only 25 per cent of F-35 fighters can fully complete all their missions, meaning that at any given time, three out of every four aircraft are either facing operational limitations or are grounded. Rapid development has severely strained the fleet support system, which was already facing problems such as delays in software updates, spare parts shortages and obsolescence. Solving these problems is expected to cost 13.7 billion dollars.
